Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed up 0.5%, Shanghai down 0.0%.

The S&P 500 is down 1.0%, the VIX up 11.1%, the DXY up 0.2%, gold down 2.2%, Brent down 1.1%, the US 10Y Yield down 0.3%, 10Y BTPs are stable.

Xi and Carney cancelled tariffs, while Putin announced a new world order with Russia. These developments reinforced risk‑off sentiment.

No significant macro data released today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above $68,000, up 0.32%. Daily net ETF flows are +$3.8 million, indicating positive institutional interest. Ethereum down 0.61%, Solana up 3.40%, surpassing the 2% significant movement threshold. BNB is almost flat, up 0.09%. Market sentiment is marked by a Fear & Greed index of eleven, classified as Extreme Fear, suggesting caution among investors. The news of a possible Bitcoin drop to $50,000, cited by Wintermute, adds uncertainty to the landscape, but it is not yet confirmed. In summary, Bitcoin shows modest growth, Solana emerges as the most dynamic altcoin, and sentiment remains extremely prudent, indicating a watchful phase for market participants.

For deeper coverage of today’s topics, find the full articles in the Spotlight Stories section on our platform. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Philippines did not deliver a South China Sea Code of Conduct. But it has shown what ASEAN can achieve
articles.snippet: The Philippines did not deliver a South China Sea Code of Conduct. But it has shown what ASEAN can achieve Expert comment jon.wallace 17 November 2026 This week’s summit did not produce the Code many desire. But as ASEAN Chair Manila has laid a useful foundation for the Code, while making important progress on regional connectivity. When it assumed the Chair of ASEAN last year, the Philippines placed negotiations to establish a South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC) at the centre of its agenda. An agreement has been desired for decades, to help reduce territorial and other tensions between China and regional countries. The need for the COC is clear: Philippine ships have continued to clash with Chinese Coast Guard vessels throughout the year, around disputed areas such as Scarborough Shoal.
